item.title: Where the Lightning has Struck, A true story about Mohawk Chief John Deserontyon — Sat Sep 12, 2:00 PM — New Toronto
item.description:
Join Pamela Devonshire as she shares her children's book, Where the Lightning Has Struck : A True Story About Mohawk Chief John Deserontyon, including why she wrote her book and why it's important to honour and remember her ancestry. Pamela will also provide information about the Haudenosaunee Confederacy and the Mohawk language, including how to say thank you in Mohawk. Children will then be invited to create their own bookmarks where they can write thank you in Mohawk or the language of their choice and share about their own culture and heritage. item.title: World Premiere Ink based on a true story at TIFF 2026 (Princess of Wales) — Tue Sep 15, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Experience Toronto Note: This is a premium performance.
**On Tuesday September 15th,** **see Ink at the 51st edition of the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF), my second choice for movies after Fjord**. Fast-paced and gripping, Boyle’s *Ink* traces the dark journalistic legacy of *The Sun* that continues to reverberate today. Director Danny Boyle (TIFF ’08’s People Choice Award winner *Slumdog Millionaire*) stylishly adapts playwright James Graham’s wild recounting of how *The Sun* became one of the most successful newspapers in British history while launching tabloid culture. I am in Dress Circle Seat D38. **Purchase Ink on Tuesday September 15th at 2:30pm.**
Rupert Murdoch (Guy Pearce, *The Brutalist*, TIFF ’24) persuades newspaper editor Larry Lamb (Jack O’Connell) to oversee his newly acquired but flagging daily, *The Sun*. But how to grab readers in the highly competitive British media market? Be extreme, throwing anything onto the page that will make a splash, the more

item.title: 🚐 Doors Open London Road Trip + Chuck's Roadhouse — Sun Sep 20, 8:00 AM
item.description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years! 🚐 **Doors Open London Road Trip!**
**Sunday, September 20**
Let’s hit the road and make a day of it! We’re heading to **[Doors Open London](https://www.londonheritage.ca/doorsopenlondon)** for a fun, curiosity-fuelled adventure exploring buildings and spaces that are usually closed to the public.
**A little context:** Nick has been a **Doors Open Toronto volunteer for over two decades** (yep, a true Doors Open nerd in the best way 😄) and genuinely loves checking out how other cities do it. London is packed with history, beautiful architecture, and some surprising hidden gems—perfect for a Doors Open day trip.
***
### 🏛️ What is Doors Open?
If you’ve never been before, Doors Open is an **annual, free architectural and cultural event** where cities open the doors to historic, cultural, and behind-the-scenes spaces. Think heritage buildings, churches, civic spaces, theatres, old industrial sites, and more—often with tours, guides
